title: Arkret Standard Event Payloads
description: Definitions bundle for common payload contracts used by registered ak.* Event.kind values. The root schema is intentionally generic and MUST NOT be used as a complete payload validator. Event validators MUST validate the full Event Envelope and dispatch by Event.kind to the matching $defs payload class using artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json.

not.$comment: The event-payload schema root is a definition-bundle diagnostic only. Standard payload validation MUST select one explicit kind-bound schema ref from the event kind registry.

account_data_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.account_data.set. Writes one holder-private account-data key; the value may be plaintext inside an already private envelope, encrypted account-data material, or a tombstone. Every key is a compare-and-set whole-value register per zh/models/account-data.md §5: expected_server_revision is the revision the writer believes is current (0 to create), and the accepted revision is expected_server_revision + 1. The object is closed: expected_revision is not an alias, and carrying both names is invalid before signature verification or storage.

body.description: Caller-supplied opaque account-data value. Any JSON value.

expected_server_revision.description: Compare-and-set precondition against the accepted per-key revision. A mismatch MUST be rejected with cas_conflict and MUST NOT be stored; the revision counter is a high-water mark that never goes backwards, so a stale offline retry cannot resurrect a superseded value. This is the Station-maintained monotone per-key counter of the server_revision_cas merge on the account-private face. It is a different mechanism from the shared face’s typed expected_revision ({commit_id, stream_position}) and carries a different name so the two can never be compared against each other.

source_pending_event_id.description: Required only for the first create of ak.agent.draft.v1:<agent_id_sha256_b64u43>:<draft_id_sha256_b64u43>. It selects the available Station-private ak.agent.draft.propose pending intent whose exact agent_id and draft_id literals are domain-separated, SHA-256 hashed and unpadded-base64url encoded to recompute the signed key before the intent is consumed atomically with the successful account-data CAS. The Station does not reverse the components and accepts no caller-supplied selector. This one-way later-submission commitment is the named forward-declaration exception in zh/conformance/encoding.md §3.1.

actor_profile_create_payload.description: Initial actor profile payload. payload.object is the closed authoring region of actor-profile.schema.json, not the materialized object; see that definition for which members the reducer produces and why.

actor_profile_update_payload.description: Actor Profile patch payload. resolution and every resolution.* descendant path are reducer-managed projections of the PCR resolution typed current result. principal_id and actor_kind are create-locked by ak.profile.create: zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md section 2.3 decides which principal a profile is for at create, and nothing said an update could not move it, so this surface could rebind a profile to another principal or retype a user as an agent. All three are forbidden here; the object-specific forbidden path set is machine-indexed in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json.

agent_action_approve_payload.description: Controller-signed security command binding one complete pre-authored Event by content-derived EventId. The canonical Event bytes exist before approval, avoiding any digest or RealmCommit self-reference. Confirmation atomically consumes the nonce and authorizes only that exact Event.

approval_nonce.description: At least 128 bits of controller-generated entropy; one immutable allocation per controller ActorId and target Realm. It cannot be released or reassigned.

expires_at.description: Inclusive confirmation deadline judged only against signed RealmCommit committed_at with zero tolerance: the covering commit of this confirmation and the covering commit of the approved Event MUST each have committed_at <= expires_at. Envelope created_at is display-only and is not compared; no Station-local current time is read.

agent_action_reject_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_reject. Controller rejection terminates one actor-private action request, named by request_id, without shared Realm side effects. A draft is not a rejection target: its workflow_state is controller-encrypted Account Data (zh/models/actor-private-effects.md section 3.2).

agent_action_request_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_request. Actor-private request for controller approval before a shared Realm write is emitted.

agent_action_target.description: Minimal target descriptor for an actor-private agent draft or approval. It identifies the eventual shared write surface without disclosing private draft content.

agent_deactivate_payload.description: Payload for the single terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Event. The lifecycle typed current result is addressed only by the complete account ActorId in envelope.actor_id using the registered canonical composite subject; the Agent principal is derived from envelope.actor_id and the controller from envelope.executed_by, so the payload carries no agent or controller coordinate mirror. executed_by and its paired authorization_ref are mandatory for this kind under the registered event-kind admission rule. At the accepted RealmCommit covering this Event, every verifier mechanically AND-gates all subordinate Agent runtime-key authorizations, sessions, pairing handles, capability grants, KeyPackages, presence and future submissions on lifecycle=active. Historical child Events remain auditable; explicit child revokes are not prerequisites and are reserved for targeted revocation while the Agent is non-terminal. The lifecycle state witness is sufficient transition evidence for every derived ineffective child.

previous_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent at deactivation time. Generic Agent status has only lifecycle, readiness and presence; pairing-poll runtime_state is operation-local and never appears here (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_draft_propose_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.draft.propose. Acceptance creates one Station-private pending intent and never creates encrypted account data. content_handoff is HPKE ciphertext for current accepted controller devices; Station cannot decrypt it.

agent_key_approval_evidence.description: Evidence that authorized this agent key: a tagged, resolvable reference to authorization provenance, not a detached signature. Durable grant/approval/policy evidence carries evidence_ref so it can be replayed at the event checkpoint; approval_event MUST resolve to a registered, accepted Agent confirmation Event (ak.agent.action_approve) and MUST NOT be read as an ak.schema.approval_signature.v1 evidence object (zh/authz/constraint-schema.md section 9.2.6). The short-lived pairing_request branch instead binds pairing_request_id, request_canonical_digest, and approved_by and MUST omit ref.

pairing_request_id.description: Optional profile-local, short-lived pairing artifact id. Required by the agent-key pairing acceptance flow and MUST equal the pairing_request_id in the accepted request; it is not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_key_authorize_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.authorize. Binds one concrete agent signing key to an accountable principal, explicit agent_key_scope, audience, validity window, approval evidence, and both the service-surface and content-capability ceilings that later agent_key_proof sessions must narrow from.

public_key.description: The complete canonical Ed25519 signing key authenticated by this Event. kid MUST equal verification_method; key decodes to exactly 32 bytes. No second controller signature or independently authored key digest exists.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the key authorization is non-expiring and governed solely by revocation (ak.agent.key.revoke / lifecycle cascade).

supersedes.description: Exact complete active authorization set at expected_revision and first acceptance, sorted byte-lexicographically by (key_id, authorized_event_ref). Omit exactly when the active set is empty, including after revoke. Each authorization Event identifies its registered add dot. Same-key reauthorization uses the same exact-set rule. Remove the observed old-key typed results atomically and add the new authorization; never infer authority from historical row presence or map overwrite.

revocation_check_ref.description: Optional freshness source for revocation checking. When expires_at is absent, authorization lifetime is governed by the canonical revocation chain and lifecycle cascade; this field may identify the freshness source used for that check.

runtime_attestation.description: Optional runtime / workload attestation captured at pairing approval time. v1 enum includes self_asserted as baseline; future profiles MAY register TEE / SLSA / SPIFFE attestation kinds. Implementations encountering an unknown kind MUST fail closed.

kind.description: v1 enum. Future profiles MAY extend via accepted attestation taxonomy.

attestation_ref.description: Optional content-addressed reference to exact external verifiable attestation bytes (TEE quote, SLSA provenance, etc.). Its embedded suite and digest are the sole wire commitment to that material.

agent_key_id.description: Stable key identifier within the agent DID. Prefer the DID URL verification method id when available.

agent_key_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.revoke. The keyed-set projection typed current result subject is (agent_id, key_id); future protocol proofs from this key fail closed once this event is covered by an accepted RealmCommit. The authoring checkpoints is the current authority-committed state; the payload carries no checkpoint field.

agent_key_scope.description: Agent scope object with two uses. In POST /_arkret/self/agents requested_scope it is the required immutable global Agent ceiling; in ak.agent.key.authorize it is a per-key ceiling that MAY be narrower but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of the provision ceiling. It is never a capability grant. actions may contain service operation ids and content action tokens; an omitted action can never be restored by a key, Realm grant or session. resources constrain the service surface and may optionally narrow later content resources, but never authorize content by themselves. Provisioning and pairing do not materialize capability grants from this object; effective authority is the intersection of provision ceiling, key ceiling, independent Realm-scoped grants, session request, membership and policy, with participation applied as an additional deny gate.

actions.description: Literal action ceiling. Every downstream key scope, grant or session action MUST appear here; action families, prefixes and subsumption do not widen it.

resources.description: Selector ceiling, not authorization. Each downstream selector must be covered by a parent selector. operation/service parents cover the same kind and matching explicit field and cannot carry content fields. The content-kind vocabulary is the ResourceSelector vocabulary except '*'; kind=realm covers every Realm-local content kind in the matching Realm and other content kinds cover only the same kind. Omitted parent realm_id is a cross-Realm ceiling wildcard and omitted exact ref is a same-kind/same-Realm wildcard. With no content selector, later Realm grants still choose concrete resources and no content wildcard is granted.

constraints.description: Global mandatory constraints. Every effective key/grant/session evaluation MUST retain and AND these constraints; downstream scopes may add stricter constraints but MUST NOT omit or relax provision constraints.

agent_pause_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.pause. The status typed current result is keyed by the complete account ActorId in envelope.actor_id using the registered canonical composite subject and moves from active to paused; the Agent principal is derived from envelope.actor_id and the controller from envelope.executed_by, so the payload carries no agent or controller coordinate mirror. executed_by and its paired authorization_ref are mandatory for this kind under the registered event-kind admission rule. Authorization is evaluated against the current authority-committed state; the reducer accepts the transition only under the accepted current authority-committed results.

agent_resume_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.resume. The status typed current result is keyed by the complete account ActorId in envelope.actor_id using the registered canonical composite subject; the Agent principal is derived from envelope.actor_id and the controller from envelope.executed_by, so the payload carries no agent or controller coordinate mirror. executed_by and its paired authorization_ref are mandatory for this kind under the registered event-kind admission rule. Authorization is evaluated against the current authority-committed state, and reducers re-check controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant against the accepted current authority-committed results before returning the agent to active. Sidecar desired membership is derived afterward and is not carried in this payload.

agent_sidecar_exchange_control_payload.description: Outer payload for ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. sidecar_id and source_context_ref route the Event inside a native Sidecar scope; encrypted_payload plaintext MUST validate as agent-sidecar-exchange-control.schema.json. Admission MUST require matching scope_ref.kind=sidecar and actor_id equal to the Sidecar controller.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped Agent label slug. Not a free-text mention address, global handle, or authorization subject.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Closed visibility scope enum for the error event. Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / Realm-policy-authorized administrator actor and checked by the Station authorization capability. The formal Event is signed by that installing administrator and admitted by the target Station; payload.proof is the exact controller-signed package proof and is not an Event proof.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet identifier; service identity is carried separately in service_id.

service_id.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_principal_id.description: Accountable human or organization publisher principal that signs the registration; the runtime service_id is not an eligible controller.

claimed_profiles.description: Canonical Applet implementation profiles copied from the accepted package. These durable claims are the authority source for profile-bound grant rules.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

webhook_auth.description: Transaction push HTTP signature policy copied from the Applet package. webhook_auth.key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used to verify the app/bridge->arkret inbound HTTP message signature and is bound to this registration_epoch; node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service DID from Source-Service-ID instead.

manifest.description: Closed package-derived manifest and the sole registration-epoch evidence carrier.

proof.description: Exact controller-DID detached package proof copied from the accepted Applet package. payload_digest binds the canonical package, while the enclosing formal registration Event has its own unique producer proof and signer-resolution evidence.

audience_mention_node.description: Broadcast mention AST node carried in a Content Block `audience_mentions[]`. It is never expanded into `mention_node` entries in shared history; recipient expansion happens receiver-side under the ak.message.mention.broadcast, audience policy, max_recipients and quota gates in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3-§9.4.4.

audience.description: Canonical audience selector. @here maps to strand_engaged and is never presence-filtered; presence-filtered audiences require a separate declared profile.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ak.audit.accessed. It binds the writer, logical target and any paired Event. The current governance Station evaluates the access against committed typed state; no typed current result or caller-authored state-head digest is carried.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event recorded by this audit marker. The marker is not historical membership proof, an epoch-to-commit proof, a decrypt-success receipt, or authorization to reveal plaintext. Ordinary verified MLS pending-decrypt retry remains separate.

board_space_id.description: A Space with kind=board. Pattern matches any ak:space:; kind invariant enforced by reducer/profile.

call_participant.description: A single participant value added by ak.call.state.payload.roster_delta. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

participant_id.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg.

participant_binding.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg. The containing call focus.mode selects the semantic branch.

focus_id.description: Required with an SFU/MCU participant binding, absent for P2P/mesh. Freeze the selected focus in this roster entry so later focus changes cannot alter its signature input.

call_recording_start_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.recording.start. recording_id is a stable opaque ASCII handle (1–128 bytes, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) that feeds the recording key exporter Context byte-for-byte and MUST NOT be normalized by receivers. capture_kind selects recording vs transcription so both lifecycles share one start event kind. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5 / §5.1.

recording_id.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript lifecycle handle. Canonical byte-for-byte; receivers MUST NOT normalize (case-fold, NFC/NFKC, trim, re-encode) because it is a cross-implementation key-derivation input.

capture_kind.description: Whether this start event opens a recording or a transcription segment. REQUIRED: it selects the target capture typed current result family (call_recording vs call_transcript) in the registered typed current result contract, so it MUST NOT be inferred from a missing-field default.

visible_notice.description: Asserts the initiating client will display the capture-in-progress notice to all participants.

result.description: Initial immutable capture evidence. retention.consent_confirmed=true closes the pre-capture consent gate before the FSM enters a capturing state. This wire payload MUST NOT carry recording_start_event_id or transcript_start_event_id: the accepted Event identity is derived only after digesting this payload, and the reducer stamps that identity into the projected result typed current result.

call_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.call.create. call_id is omitted and derived by retyping the accepted Event id. Signaling, media tokens, Morph bindings, and state deltas MUST reference only an already accepted create.

call_state_payload.description: Typed delta payload for ak.call.state. Every present field maps to one or two explicit registered typed current result effects; omitted axes produce no effect.

failure_reason_code.description: Machine reason for to="failed". Required when to="failed" and forbidden otherwise, so a failed call always carries a diagnostic and a non-failed transition cannot smuggle one.

result.description: Ordinary capture outcome details. Result status is derived from to and stored with these details. Ready/failed require the exact confirmed stop Event for the same call, segment, capture authority and generation; they cannot modify permission or key access.

artifact.description: Canonical artifact metadata for recording_transition.to=ready. It binds the Arkret blob, recording exporter context, retention policy and deletion audit surface.

failure_message.description: Human-readable diagnostic for recording_state=failed. It MUST NOT contain recording plaintext or backend direct URLs.

result.description: Ordinary capture outcome details. Result status is derived from to and stored with these details. Ready/failed require the exact confirmed stop Event for the same call, segment, capture authority and generation; they cannot modify permission or key access.

expected_revision.description: Exact current call-roster revision observed by the producer. It is the typed revision of the value the producer read, so the compare-and-set names the same {commit_id, stream_position} the typed current result carries. A producer-chosen integer would be a producer-side order, which the authority-commit model does not have.

Exact current moderation revision for this participant observed by the producer. It is the typed revision of the value the producer read, so the compare-and-set names the same {commit_id, stream_position} the typed current result carries. A producer-chosen integer would be a producer-side order, which the authority-commit model does not have.

capability_grant_payload.description: Canonical ak.capability.grant genesis payload. Both top-level grant_id and grant.id are forbidden because the durable GrantId is derived by retyping this Event's event_id. status, authority_depth and authority_root_refs are reducer-derived and forbidden in this closed authoring shape. issuer_id and a concrete subject are already exact ActorIds; no parallel Station sidecar is permitted. issuer_authority_refs is signed semantic lineage and cannot carry expected_revision, auth_state_digest or a Station-local commit basis; current authority is checked by the governing Station at acceptance. The Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature.

capability_relinquish_payload.description: ak.capability.relinquish — subject-only release of the actor own grant. The authority is the target grant subject's signature, never a capability: a narrowly-scoped holder that was never granted ak.capability.revoke must still be able to give up what it holds. The reducer target guard accepts actor == target.subject and nothing else, so this can never become an unauthorized revocation. Descendants of the released grant fail through their issuer_authority_refs at read time.

expected_revision.description: It is the typed revision of the value the producer read, so the compare-and-set names the same {commit_id, stream_position} the typed current result carries. A producer-chosen integer would be a producer-side order, which the authority-commit model does not have.

It is the typed revision of the value the producer read, so the compare-and-set names the same {commit_id, stream_position} the typed current result carries. A producer-chosen integer would be a producer-side order, which the authority-commit model does not have.

circle_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the create branch of Circle schema. Reducer requires created_by/created_at to match the Event, derives circle_id and, once the Circle scope has an accepted ak.mls.genesis, derives mls_group_id. A Circle is created plaintext and carries no encryption profile, content scheme or encryption floor. Actor-supplied id or mls_group_id is forbidden.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

circle_member_state_payload.description: Payload for ak.circle.member.state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ak.member.state (Realm), scoped to a Circle; reducer MUST verify member_id is a `join` member of the parent Realm before any transition to `join`, MUST gate `knock` on Circle join_rule=knock, and MUST reject self-unban/self-unremove paths.

expected_membership.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard, orthogonal to the membership transition guard. The three wire states are distinct: omission applies no CAS and leaves legality to the FSM guard, explicit null asserts the actor currently has no membership record in this Circle, and a concrete value asserts the current membership equals it. A failed assertion MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

circle_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.circle.update. Patch path MUST NOT contain realm_id, mls_group_id, history_access, state, state_changed_at, created_by, or created_at; history_access changes use dedicated ak.circle.history_access. Reducer enforces create-locks and semantic policy checks.

consent_peer.description: Closed consent counterparty identity. Ordinary accounts, Agents, pseudonymous accounts and MIMI-correlated parties use one exact ActorId, including Account Station and actor role.

consent_grant_payload.description: Holder-private consent grant evaluated in the holder's Principal Control Realm. consent_id is the stable domain identity and the governance Station serializes changes on the PCR Realm stream.

consent_id.description: Stable identifier; used as the result_selector of the consent typed current result. ak.consent.revoke MUST reference the same consent_id.

consent_scope.description: What kind of contact is consented to. 'invite' = peer may send Realm / Strand invites; 'direct_message' = peer may initiate 1:1 message; 'voice_call' / 'video_call' = peer may initiate WebRTC call; 'presence' = peer may observe presence; 'any' = full consent across all consent scopes.

constraints.description: Optional consent-specific constraints (rate limits, time-of-day windows, device restrictions). v1 does not standardise constraint types beyond capability constraint vocabulary.

evidence_ref.description: Optional reference to claim disclosure, presentation response, or invite proof that triggered this consent (audit trail).

consent_revoke_payload.description: Revoke the current consent identified by consent_id at exactly expected_revision. The governance Station rejects a stale revision and applies an accepted Event in stream order.

consent_id.description: MUST equal the consent_id of the ak.consent.grant being revoked.

expected_revision.description: Exact current consent revision observed by the producer. It is the typed revision of the value the producer read, so the compare-and-set names the same {commit_id, stream_position} the typed current result carries. A producer-chosen integer would be a producer-side order, which the authority-commit model does not have.

contact_accepted_payload.description: Holder-signed normal Contact acceptance fact. This is version 1 of the issuer-local directional lineage. It grants only the explicit Contact scopes and neither reads nor writes Consent.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Required by semantic admission when the accepted request is a recontact. It MUST equal the same field in the referenced request fact and its source-signed acceptance receipt. It is absent for a root Contact round.

contact_rejected_payload.description: Holder-signed terminal rejection of one exact accepted request. It establishes no Contact round and carries no Consent or Contact round evidence fields.

contact_requested_payload.description: Requester-signed directional Contact request fact. It is created before any acceptance receipt or contact round exists, so neither may appear in this payload. It grants only the requester's explicit Contact scopes and neither reads nor writes Consent.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Required digest of the exact private introduction_evidence carried by the request branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1. Raw evidence is not written into the contact fact log.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Requester-signed immediate predecessor link for recontact. It is required when this request follows a previously accepted terminal Contact round and forbidden for a root request. It is not the issuer-local request-slot predecessor.

contact_tombstoned_payload.description: Holder-signed terminal event for one issuer-local Contact lineage. The event kind itself supplies terminal semantics; the payload carries only the exact peer, contact round and predecessor coordinates. It does not read, write or revoke Consent.

mentions.description: Structured direct mention AST nodes for this Content Block. This is the only carrier of a direct mention: authorization, notification routing and audit attribution read mention_node.subject_account_id exclusively, and compare it as a complete AccountId (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.1-§9.4.2).

audience_mentions.description: Structured broadcast mention AST nodes for this Content Block (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3).

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field name `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`. The discriminator is `kind`, the composite child array is `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes` (see schemas/message.schema.json and forbidden-wire-fields.json `blocks/content_block_composite`).

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

content_block_long_text.description: ak.content.long_text: plain text whose full normalized UTF-8 body exceeds the 256 KiB inline boundary (or, by the narrow exception in zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4, whose Event would otherwise exceed the 1 MiB envelope limit). Exactly one of the plaintext branch (blob_ref + size_bytes + media_type) and the E2EE branch (attachment) applies. v1 core Content Block: no feature gate, no server-side opt-out.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

blob_ref.description: Hash-addressed Blob ref for the full normalized UTF-8 body. UUID blob refs are forbidden here because they carry no digest commitment.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 body bytes. The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4), not a schema minimum.

media_type.description: Full-body media type and sole rendering discriminator. No parameters: charset is fixed to UTF-8 by this kind.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

attachment.description: Encrypted full-body Blob descriptor. MUST use scheme ak.blob.stream_aead.v1 with the matching _stream alg; whole-file AEAD is forbidden for long text.

blob_ref.description: Long text MUST use a content-addressed Blob ref; its embedded <suite>:<hex> is the attachment's only ciphertext digest carrier and MUST equal the independent Blob metadata content_digest.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 plaintext body bytes. The segment count is derived as max(1, ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes)) and never carried on wire. The >256 KiB rule and narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules.

media_type.description: Full-body media type and sole rendering discriminator. No parameters: charset is fixed to UTF-8 by this kind.

cross_object_redaction_payload.description: Payload for the cross-object ak.redaction. Shares the object_redaction typed current result family with ak.message.redact but carries a target set that mechanically excludes Message: message_id is not a member and target_ref cannot spell ak:message:. target_ref is the single target carrier; its lexical space covers both object targets and ak:event: targets, so the typed current result subject is well defined without a coalesce.

cross_object_redaction_target_ref.description: Cross-object ak.redaction object target. Identical to object_ref except that ak:message: is removed from the typed-object alternation: Message is the only object with a registered object-scoped redact kind, so a Message MUST enter state=redacted through ak.message.redact and MUST NOT be the target of a cross-object ak.redaction (models/common-fields.md 5.2).

device_authorize_payload.description: Closed authorization record shared by registration genesis, PCR-policy recovery, accepted-device pairing, and Applet-managed delegation. Its exact AccountId subject is derived exclusively from the Event envelope actor_id; the payload MUST NOT mirror a principal_id. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use a candidate-device possession proof over the full authorization core bound to that exact AccountId; pcr_recovery is admitted only beside an accepted recovery session and monotonic PCR generation CAS. accepted_device uses the current accepted approving device. applet_managed_delegation is an ordinary successor Event inside an already accepted applet_managed_control PCR, signed by that principal's own controller method resolved from its accepted current resolution typed current result, so it needs no unit-local candidate overlay. None of these branches derives human authority from current DID state.

hpke_key.description: Device HPKE public key used for secret/key envelope encryption. It is covered by the possession transcript and by the surrounding root anchor or accepted-device Event proof; services MUST NOT substitute it. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_proof, which the approving device reads only after that attestation verifies.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids supported by this device. Enters device trust binding transcript together with device_public_key_did and hpke_key. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_proof, not any service-supplied or staged copy.

authorized_by.description: Under registration_anchor this is the principal whose durable registration control evidence was accepted. Under pcr_recovery it is the same principal selected by the recovery session and account-local lineage. Under accepted_device it is the approving device id at the accepted generation. Under applet_managed_delegation it is the Applet-managed principal's own principal_id, equal to actor_id.account_id.principal_id: the managed PCR authorizes its own delegated device and no cross-principal authority is introduced.

authorization_binding_kind.description: registration_anchor is valid only in accepted PCR genesis; pcr_recovery only in a recovery unit authorized by the accepted PCR recovery policy; accepted_device requires an active approving device; applet_managed_delegation is valid only as an ordinary successor Event inside an accepted applet_managed_control PCR and only while the exact Applet install that created that principal is still active. No branch permits a same-core foreign PCR lineage.

authorized_generation_ref.description: PCR-local device generation this authorization is bound to, carried on the wire and verified by the accepting side with one equality against already committed state (device-lifecycle.md section 5.5.2). registration_anchor MUST carry 1, the value the same pcr_genesis_unit initializes; pcr_recovery MUST equal the sibling ak.device.reanchor new_device_generation; accepted_device and applet_managed_delegation MUST equal the PCR's current_device_generation_ref at acceptance. It is NOT a reducer pre-state read: v1's two derivation vocabularies admit only pure functions of this Event plus the two authority-root successor counters whose pre-state an expected_state_digest CAS freezes, and this Event has no such freeze. Self-reporting it does not contradict the ak.device.revoke rule against self-reported derived pending selectors: that rule covers selectors only the reducer produces inside its own transaction, while this one is decided before acceptance by a single equality. It is not and MUST NOT be derived from a DID versionId. It is covered by the registration_anchor / pcr_recovery / applet_managed_delegation possession transcripts, whose shared device_authorize_possession_core registers it as a signed member; those transcripts cover the authorization core plus the injected account_id and exclude every signature and digest member of this payload, so they are not an allOf of this payload. The accepted_device device_pairing_target_proof is a closed eight-member object that deliberately excludes it, and the approving device's Event proof over the full canonical Event bytes covers it instead.

device_signature.description: Required Ed25519 possession proof. It is the output of a possession transcript and therefore never a member of one. registration_anchor signs device_authorize_possession_transcript under ak.device_authorize_possession_proof.v1; pcr_recovery signs device_authorize_recovery_possession_transcript under ak.device_authorize_recovery_possession_proof.v1; applet_managed_delegation signs device_authorize_applet_managed_possession_transcript under ak.device_authorize_applet_managed_possession_proof.v1, the same device_authorize_possession_core plus applet_id; accepted_device carries the single device_pairing_target_proof signature over the full challenge descriptor bound to the final AccountId and authorization core. The accepted-device branch MUST verify pairing_challenge_transcript_digest against that signed descriptor; no second new-device signature is required.

recovery_session_id.description: Required by the pcr_recovery branch and omitted for registration_anchor, ordinary accepted_device pairing and applet_managed_delegation.

pairing_challenge_transcript_digest.description: Required only for accepted_device. SHA-256 typed digest of the complete canonical challenge descriptor authenticated by device_signature; the verifier persists the descriptor and rechecks the exact final AccountId and authorization core.

applet_id.description: Required only for applet_managed_delegation and forbidden on every other branch. The exact Applet install whose accepted managed-actor provision created this principal. It is the device's revocation fence: once that install is revoked the device MUST stop being an effective signer, so the binding cannot outlive the install that justified it.

device_push_route_payload.description: Closed account-private push-route write. Active routes and revoked tombstones are mutually exclusive whole-value shapes and both carry the single server-revision CAS precondition. The account identity is one atomic AccountId; its Station is never repeated as a delivery field.

expected_server_revision.description: This is the Station-maintained monotone per-key counter of the server_revision_cas merge on the account-private face. It is a different mechanism from the shared face’s typed expected_revision ({commit_id, stream_position}) and carries a different name so the two can never be compared against each other.

This is the Station-maintained monotone per-key counter of the server_revision_cas merge on the account-private face. It is a different mechanism from the shared face’s typed expected_revision ({commit_id, stream_position}) and carries a different name so the two can never be compared against each other.

device_reanchor_payload.description: Closed account-local PCR recovery payload. The account authority is selected by the exact AccountId and one monotonic local device-generation CAS. PCR realm/checkpoint identifiers remain local recovery state and are not an external principal identity selector.

new_device_generation.description: Must be the immediate monotonic successor of previous_device_generation.

did_root_evidence_digest.description: Required only when recovery_authority_kind=did_root; proves the optional factor enabled by the frozen PCR policy.

replacement_authorize_payload_digest.description: canonical_digest of the replacement ak.device.authorize payload object, using the Realm live digest suite.

device_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.device.revoke. Its exact AccountId subject is derived exclusively from the Event envelope actor_id; the payload MUST NOT mirror a principal_id. The revocation's control-plane authorization basis is the current authority-committed state (covered by the canonical Event bytes and producer_proof); its permanent cutoff is the accepted RealmCommit covering this Event. First durable canonical acceptance atomically creates ak.schema.device_revocation_state.v1 revocation_pending for the exact reducer-derived current device authorization and generation. The payload carries no checkpoint or generation field, and producers cannot self-report derived pending selectors.

direct_conversation_authorization_basis.description: Canonical authorization basis for creating a Direct Conversation. accepted_contact carries exactly the accepted contact request/accept refs. agent_controller carries exactly two unique accepted Event refs: the controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event, whose payload already binds the Agent, controller, delegation, accountability and selector facts, and the current active ak.agent.key.authorize Event.

direct_conversation_bound_payload.description: Participant endorsement of the settled Direct Conversation coordinates and the first exact-pair state in the scope's single immutable derived MLS group. It does not enforce uniqueness: at most one Realm can exist per pair because only the founder derived from the pair's root Contact round may author the founding unit. What the first accepted write settles is the BINDING CONTENT -- a later endorsement carrying a different semantic binding_digest is refused before projection -- not the membership of the result: contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 8.3 makes this a set-shaped collection, and the second participant endorsement of the same binding MUST be acceptable. binding_digest is a receiver-derived off-wire semantic digest over the closed normalized binding object defined by contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 8.3 and MUST NOT be added to this payload.

pair_key.description: Canonical unordered pair key: SHA-256(UTF8(ak.direct-conversation.pair-key.v1 followed by LF) || JCS({participants:[p0,p1],trust_domain_id})) where p0/p1 are exact ActorIds sorted by their RFC 8785 JCS bytes. Receivers MUST recompute it exactly as contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 5.1 defines; handles, bare principal IDs and unresolved pairwise DIDs are forbidden inputs.

founding_unit_digest.description: Digest of the accepted four Event atomic founding unit this binding endorses.

initial_exact_pair_group_state_ref.description: The winning Add Commit Event that first establishes both exact participants in the scope's single immutable derived MLS group.

history_access_payload.description: Realm history-access FSM transition. The atomic create unit uses from=null exactly once and chooses either closed initial state. After create the only legal state-changing edge is all_history_for_current_members to since_join; widening and every other new transition are permanently rejected. Exact same-transition/same-basis replay is an idempotent duplicate/no-op.

circle_history_access_payload.description: Dedicated per-Circle history-access FSM transition. Circle create initializes from=null. The only post-create edge is all_history_for_current_members to since_join; exact replay is idempotent and widening is permanently rejected. Generic ak.circle.update patches cannot touch history_access.

discovery_profile_visibility.description: Explicit map from profile field name to its maximum directory disclosure class. Dynamic keys are confined to this declared map slot.

invitee_account_id.description: Exact directed invite account. The Invite id is derived from this Event's event_id and MUST NOT be carried in the genesis payload. Delivery resolves this AccountId's station_id outside durable Realm state.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

expires_at.description: Invite expiry timestamp. Directed v1 invite creates MUST carry it; reducers MUST NOT infer indefinite validity.

third_party_invite.description: Third-party invite genesis material. The Invite id is derived from this Event's event_id and MUST NOT be carried in the payload.

previous_state.description: The invite_lifecycle state this Event expects to move out of. zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 gives this kind several legal source states, so the registered transition projection reads its from endpoint here instead of pinning one const and dropping the rest -- the same shape agent_deactivate_payload uses for previous_status. It is a declared pre-state, not a producer-side order: the reducer compares it with the frozen pre-state at admission and rejects a mismatch, which is what stops an Event authored against a pending Invite from landing on a claimed one.

invitee_account_id.description: Present exactly when the target Invite stores one, that is for a directed invite and never for a third-party invite; admission compares it byte-for-byte with the stored value. It is the only signed source from which the invite_live_target slot subject can be derived, because the reducer projection grammar cannot convert the envelope ActorId into an AccountId.

previous_state.description: The invite_lifecycle state this Event expects to move out of. zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 gives this kind several legal source states, so the registered transition projection reads its from endpoint here instead of pinning one const and dropping the rest -- the same shape agent_deactivate_payload uses for previous_status. It is a declared pre-state, not a producer-side order: the reducer compares it with the frozen pre-state at admission and rejects a mismatch, which is what stops an Event authored against a pending Invite from landing on a claimed one.

invitee_account_id.description: MUST equal the directed invite's stored exact account so invite_lifecycle and member_state move atomically.

reason_code.description: Optional supplementary diagnostic for the transition this Event carries. The cause is already fixed by the Event kind and target_state (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3), so admission never decides legality from it. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes; reason stays free text for humans.

previous_state.description: The invite_lifecycle state this Event expects to move out of. zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3 gives this kind several legal source states, so the registered transition projection reads its from endpoint here instead of pinning one const and dropping the rest -- the same shape agent_deactivate_payload uses for previous_status. It is a declared pre-state, not a producer-side order: the reducer compares it with the frozen pre-state at admission and rejects a mismatch, which is what stops an Event authored against a pending Invite from landing on a claimed one.

invitee_account_id.description: Present exactly when the target Invite stores one and target_state is not send_failed; forbidden for a 3PID placeholder and forbidden on send_failed. It is the only signed source from which the invite_live_target slot subject can be derived, and send_failed keeps the invite inside the live set, so that transition derives no slot write and needs no account.

target_state.description: Terminal invalidation of a pending invite, carried by an authorized writer's signed Event. send_failed and expired are observations the writer commits explicitly (third-party-invites.md 6.1); neither may be written by a local timer or delivery retry loop.

reason_code.description: Optional supplementary diagnostic for the transition this Event carries. The cause is already fixed by the Event kind and target_state (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3), so admission never decides legality from it. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes; reason stays free text for humans.

invite_claim_binding_proof.description: Verification-service proof for ak.invite.claim. Reducers verify signature over the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript against the invite's verification_public_key and current Realm verification_id allowlist before accepting a claimed transition.
invite_claim_binding_proof.$comment: A malformed or unverifiable binding proof is recorded with the authorized audit reason claim_invalid; external responses stay non-enumerable (see zh/sync/third-party-invites.md §4.3 / §6).

verification_id.description: Verification service DID. Realm reducers MUST re-check this DID against the current effective Realm allowlist and any service DID pinned by the original invite.

verification_method.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0; matches the strict form used by $defs/verification_method elsewhere in this schema.

subject_account_id.description: Exact account being bound by the verification service. MUST equal the payload top-level subject_account_id.

realm_id.description: Realm bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the Event envelope realm_id.

claim_nonce.description: Nonce bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the payload top-level claim_nonce.

expires_at.description: Proof expiration. Reducers MUST reject expired proofs and MUST also enforce the invite typed current result expires_at.

signature.description: Signature over utf8("ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json({audience, binding_proof: unsigned_binding_proof, claim_nonce, invite_digest, invite_id, realm_id, subject_account_id, token_commitment, verification_id}); unsigned_binding_proof is this object without signature.

subject_account_id.description: Exact account being bound by an ak.invite.claim payload. It MUST match the account carried by binding_proof and the subject proof author; neither component may be inferred.

token_commitment.description: Reducer-matched salted commitment for the pending ak.invite.third_party record. Raw invite tokens, URL fragments, SMS codes, or plaintext 3PID values MUST NOT appear on wire.

claim_nonce.description: One-time nonce scoped to (invite_id, token_commitment). Reducers MUST reject nonce replay while preserving non-enumerable external responses.

subject_proof.description: Account holder proof over ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript. The transcript digest binds subject_account_id, invite_id, realm_id, token_commitment, claim_nonce, audience, verification_id, and binding_proof_digest of the complete signed binding_proof object.

verification_method.description: Current verification method of subject_account_id.principal_id; the admission context separately binds the exact station_id.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the canonical ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript.

join_gate_proof.description: Closed applicant-supplied proof for one automatic join gate (zh/governance/join-policy.md section 4 rule 4). The binding tuple gate_id / realm_id / applicant_actor_id / policy_digest / created_at is carried as wire members and covered by the detached proof, so a proof replayed across Realms, applicants or policy revisions fails by field comparison before any signature is checked. realm_id MUST equal the enclosing membership_payload.realm_id and applicant_actor_id MUST equal member_id; policy_digest is sha256 over the canonical JSON of the accepted join_policy component the reducer evaluates against. Freshness is judged against the enclosing Event's signed created_at, never a receiver clock: created_at + max_proof_age < event created_at is challenge_expired, created_at > event created_at is challenge_proof_invalid.
join_gate_proof.$comment: proofs[] is the shared detached-proof leaf under the registered context ak.join_gate_proof.v1 (proof-context-registry.json); payload_digest is sha256 over this object without proofs. For kind=challenge_response the signing verification_method MUST resolve, through the registered DID method adapter, to a key controlled by the gate's provider_did; for kind=claim_required it MUST resolve to a key controlled by issuer_id, and issuer_id MUST be listed in the gate's trusted_issuer_ids. parent_membership, principal_admission and cooldown gates take no proof item; a proof whose kind differs from the referenced gate's kind, or whose gate_id names no gate in the accepted policy, fails as gate_check_failed for a non-member caller.

challenge_kind.description: challenge_response only. MUST be one of the referenced gate's challenge_kinds[].

challenge_id.description: challenge_response only. Provider-scoped identifier of the solved challenge; the provider MUST treat it as single-use.

issuer_id.description: claim_required only. Issuer of the presented claims; MUST be listed in the referenced gate's trusted_issuer_ids.

claims.description: claim_required only. Claim names the issuer attests for applicant_actor_id; MUST be a superset of the referenced gate's required_claims[].

trusted_issuer_ids.description: Issuer boundary of the claim presentation, same carrier name as grant-constraint required_claims[].trusted_issuer_ids (authz/capabilities.md). A join_gate_proof for this gate MUST name an issuer_id in this list; a gate without an issuer boundary is not verifiable and is therefore not constructible.

kind.description: Realm-local admission gate evaluated only when every source Realm and the target Realm have the same verified current authority-tenure service_id and the target has an active join_gate_from link to each source. Each Realm's governance_generation must independently be current and generation numbers are not compared across Realms. The Station reads authoritative current member_state rows in the accepting transaction; all dependencies must be available and at least one source must be joined. Cross-Station, cached, replicated, historical, directory, or caller-supplied membership evidence fails closed.

join_policy_component.$comment: Value shape of the join_policy component of realm_policy_bundle_payload; it has no separate Event kind and no separate typed current result family, and rides inside the realm_policy_bundle commit-ordered projection value. Structural validation is JSON Schema; property-level gate_id uniqueness within gates[] cannot be expressed in pure JSON Schema 2020-12, so it is enforced by (a) reducer rejection with reason_code=join_policy_duplicate_gate_id and (b) tools/artifact_lint check_join_policy_gate_id_uniqueness over fixtures and Markdown examples. uniqueItems below catches whole-object duplicates as a baseline. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §3 / §3.1.

join_policy_gate_id.description: Stable gate identifier, unique within one join policy gates[]. Both the definition site and the reference site join_gate_proof.gate_id MUST use this one definition so the two lexical spaces cannot drift; a proof's gate_id MUST equal the gate_id of a gate in the accepted policy. The pattern is the document_local_symbol floor of common-fields.md 2.1: it mechanically excludes the ak: namespace that typed_object_id and responsibility_did own exclusively. See zh/governance/join-policy.md 3.1.

key_backup_active_series_payload.description: Payload for ak.key_backup.active_series. The standalone ak.schema.key_backup_active_series.v1 schema carries the authoritative signed active-series record shape.

member_identity_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.member.identity.update. Append-only replacement event for one Realm-scoped member display/subject projection segment. Service-visible metadata names the segment and the prior events it replaces; the segment body is plaintext or the original encrypted envelope and MUST contain the complete data for that segment. Handle lifecycle is excluded from this event and is governed by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims.

segment.description: v1 core defines a single full MemberIdentity segment. Narrower segments require a future schema/profile revision that extends this enum or defines a new payload schema; v1 receivers MUST reject unknown segment values.
segment.$comment: Reducer rejection for a segment value outside the v1 enum carries reason member_identity_unknown_segment. See zh/sync/client-sync.md §8.1.

replaces.description: Prior ak.member.identity.update events in the same (realm_id, actor_id, segment) that this event supersedes for current profile projection. Referenced events remain immutable history.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the replaced event's full payload.identity_payload carrier wrapper ({member_identity: ...} or {encrypted_payload: ...}). Prevents replacing a different payload under a reused or confused event id.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard for the current effective set of this (realm_id, member_id, segment). When present, it MUST equal sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the array of the exact signed payload objects of every update in that effective set, ordered by carrying event_id ascending (the empty set is []), before applying this event (zh/sync/current-results.md section 2); a mismatch is member_identity_state_mismatch with zero writes. It is distinct from the locally derived identity_payload carrier digest and from a roster member_display_state_digest.

member_id.description: Exact member identity. All Station-hosted principals, including human, Agent, Ghost and integration actors, use the AccountId-bearing account variant; directly authoring services use the service variant.

gate_proofs.description: Closed join-policy gate proofs evaluated by governance/join-policy.md section 4 before accepting membership=join. At most one item per gate_id (a duplicate gate_id is schema_violation); only challenge_response and claim_required gates take an applicant-supplied proof, the other three kinds are replayed from accepted state. maxItems aligns with the gates 1..16 bound in join_policy_component; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.
gate_proofs.$comment: Gate failures are reported to a non-member caller uniformly as gate_check_failed in response.rejected[] (see governance/join-policy.md §4). The authorized audit reasons are challenge_failed (answer verification failed, or no proof item for a challenge_response gate), claim_invalid (claim presentation failed, or no proof item for a claim_required gate) and challenge_proof_invalid (proof signature, binding tuple, or issuer/provider key resolution failed; exceeding max_proof_age is challenge_expired instead). These audit reasons MUST NOT appear in response.rejected[].

reason.description: Bounded human-readable audit note. It never supplies membership authority or proves cascade provenance.

agent_controller_binding.description: Required by semantic admission for every Agent join and every controller-membership-ended cleanup. Non-Agent membership MUST reject it.

membership_state.description: Canonical materialized membership state enum shared by ak.member.state (Realm) and ak.circle.member.state (Circle). Invite is a separate pending workflow and is never a member state. `knock` denotes a pending self-authored join request; see governance/join-policy.md §5 and models/circle.md §9.1.

subject_account_id.description: Authoritative mention target as the complete AccountId, principal and Station component both. For Agent selectors this is the agent account, not the controller account. Equality is byte-for-byte over both components: the same principal hosted by another Station is a different subject and MUST NOT match (zh/identity/identity-handles.md §3.8, zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §9).

handle_at_time.description: Canonical handle snapshot at compose time. Audit / debug / search metadata only; renderers MUST resolve the current primary handle from subject_account_id instead (zh/identity/identity-handles.md §3.8.1-§3.8.2).

controller_subject_account_id.description: Optional audit metadata for verified known-Agent picker selections, carried as the complete controller AccountId. MUST NOT replace subject_account_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

controller_handle_at_time.description: Canonical verified controller handle snapshot from a known-Agent picker. Audit / debug / search metadata only; not a free-text resolver input.

mimi_message_provenance.description: External attribution for a message Event authored and signed by a MIMI facade service. This object never transfers the attributed sender's signing authority to the facade.

message_create_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.create. If content/encrypted_content contains an audience_mention AST node (for example @all or @here), reducer admission and notification dispatch MUST additionally enforce ak.message.mention.broadcast plus the audience policy / max_recipient / rate-limit rules in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered.

allOf.$comment: ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. Reducer initializes revision_root := id on create; only ak.message.revise events may set it. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `revision_root/message_create_payload`.

ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry message_id. The materialized Message.id is obtained by retyping the creating Event.event_id's full 33-byte / 44-character token; a second identity would create a conflicting truth source. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `message_id/message_create_payload`.

reply_to_id.description: Optional creation convenience: the message this one replies to. The reducer records it as the message's reply linkage (lifting it onto the message content) and surfaces it as a replies_to relation in the message projection; it does not require a separate canonical ak.relation event. The materialized Message object itself carries no reply_to scalar. See strand-and-message.md §9.1.

agent_context.description: Auditable authorization context required when an Agent authors the message.

poll_response_heads.description: Each entry binds a poll to the exact response Event being superseded.

message_encrypted_content.description: MLS-protected Message ContentBlock bound to its one canonical decrypted schema.

message_encrypted_metadata.description: MLS-protected Message metadata bound to its one canonical decrypted schema.

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

message_redact_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.redact, the object-scoped redact kind registered for Message. Message is the only object that enters state=redacted through its own kind rather than a cross-object ak.redaction, which is why message.schema.json materializes redaction_ref (models/common-fields.md 5.2). message_id is the single target carrier, so the object_redaction typed current result subject is always the Message typed ID.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the redacted message's parent Strand. Optional: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

message_revise_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.revise. Revisions that introduce new direct mentions MAY generate mention notifications only when the implementation can compare against the previous accepted visible revision. Revisions that introduce an audience_mention AST node (including @all / @here mappings) MUST satisfy the same ak.message.mention.broadcast and policy gates as create.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the target Strand. Optional on revise/redact: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message identified by message_id. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

mimi_room_binding_payload.description: Payload for ak.mimi.room_binding. Writes the mimi_room_binding typed current result whose subject is payload.mimi_room_uri (see event-kind-registry.json result_selector). Authoritative field set: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §3. The binding is a projection of an Arkret Realm/Strand discussion track into a MIMI room; it is not canonical truth. Creation / update / revocation MUST hold ak.policy.manage, ak.realm.admin, or an equivalent interop capability. E2EE MIMI rooms MUST bind mls_group_id and pass the active MLS key_access_revision gate.

mimi_room_uri.description: Canonical MIMI room URI and the typed current result subject source for mimi_room_binding (registry result_selector.kind = uri). The closed canonical form and the full percent-encoding that turns it into a TypedResultSelector subject are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md section 4 and zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4; a non-canonical spelling MUST be rejected with schema_violation rather than normalized.

binding_scope.description: Arkret Realm + Strand scope this MIMI room projects. strand_id MUST point at an accepted Strand with discussion track enabled inside realm_id; the MIMI room timeline only projects that Strand's discussion track.

hub_provider_id.description: Service DID explicitly delegated by Realm policy, Organization DID, or participant DID to host the hub role.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group id. MUST be present for E2EE MIMI rooms.

policy_revision.description: Accepted ak.realm.policy_bundle revision this MIMI room binding projects. The facade compares it against the Realm's current committed policy revision and rejects a stale projection.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the binding. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2. accepted bindings authorize projection; revoked bindings stop new MIMI writes; migrating stops new writes until a verified migration proof returns the binding to accepted or revoked.

migration_outcome.description: Required exactly for a migrating->accepted transition, paired with migration_proof. The signed Event asserts whether the migrating candidate topology became effective or the previous accepted topology was restored.

mimi_room_binding_migration_proof.description: Commit-backed lineage proof for a migrating->accepted room-binding Event. Each Event ID MUST name an accepted ak.mimi.room_binding Event and each Commit ID MUST be its covering RealmCommit in the same Realm. Admission verifies that the migrating pair is the current typed-result source and the previous_accepted pair was the immediately preceding accepted binding state; see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

covers_key_access_revision.description: Unsigned 64-bit monotonic key-access revision covered by this Commit. It is a counter, not a digest.

group_info_ref.description: Content-addressed Blob ref. Its embedded suite prefix selects the Blob digest independently of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite.

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Content-addressed Blob ref. Its embedded suite prefix selects the Blob digest independently of the fixed SHA-256 Event/RealmCommit identity suite.

mls_governance_binding.description: The single closed Arkret MLS governance binding used identically by the Event payload, GroupContext extension 0xF1C0 and pre-Genesis proposal carrier. Five members are shared by every scope; the Sidecar scope additionally requires the signed participant authority digest and accepted authority cut, and any other scope carrying either is a schema_violation. key_access_revision is a monotonic unsigned 64-bit counter, not a digest.

key_access_revision.description: Monotonic unsigned 64-bit counter for changes to future MLS epoch key access. Equality is numeric equality; no digest alias is accepted.

authority_stream_head.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted accepted Event IDs at the exact Sidecar participant decision cut; same value as AgentSidecarView.mls_context.authority_stream_head. maxItems equals the decoder maximum_collection_items; the governance Station rejects, at acceptance time and with failed_precondition and zero writes, any authority change whose derived Sidecar cut would exceed it.

mls_genesis_binding_proposal_carrier.description: Closed local pre-Genesis proposal carrier. It identifies the future ak.mls.genesis Event route, proposal class, complete sender and target scope, and reuses the exact mls_governance_binding definition instead of declaring a second binding shape. target_scope MUST equal proposed_group_genesis_binding.effective_scope field by field; the binding MUST carry a null base_group_state_ref, previous_epoch=0, next_epoch=0 and key_access_revision=0.

moderation_decision_lift_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision.lift. The governance Station resolves decision_ref to the active decision for target_ref and applies the lift at exactly expected_revision.

target_ref.description: The moderated target whose moderation_state typed current result the lift mutates. Same typed current result subject as the original ak.moderation.decision.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the prior ak.moderation.decision Event whose committed tag is being removed.

expected_revision.description: Exact current moderation-target revision the producer observed. A different current revision rejects the Event as stale; exact retry remains idempotent. It is the typed revision of the value the producer read, so the compare-and-set names the same {commit_id, stream_position} the typed current result carries. A producer-chosen integer would be a producer-side order, which the authority-commit model does not have.

moderation_decision_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision. A committed moderation decision that writes a keyed_set_add effect onto the moderation_state typed current result whose subject is the canonical string of target_ref. Multiple active adds fold by hard_deny > quarantine > require_review > none. dismiss is valid only when target_ref identifies the report Event being closed and contributes none to the content verdict fold. Runtime allow and soft_deny remain out-of-band outcomes. The actor MUST independently hold the registered ak.moderation.decision capability.

target_ref.description: The moderated target (event / object). Canonical string of this ref is the moderation_state typed current result subject.

decision.description: committed moderation-state decision verb. dismiss only resolves a report queue item and does not loosen the target content verdict. allow and soft_deny are out-of-band runtime outcomes.

issuer_id.description: Actor or service DID issuing the committed moderation decision. It is part of the projected element VALUE, not of the element tag: a keyed_set_add tag is exactly the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot (models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2), so no payload member ever enters set identity. content-moderation.md section 5.3 folds several issuers' active records together, which is why the issuer has to survive in the value.

request_canonical_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the moderated request or Event preview. It is part of the projected element VALUE, not of the element tag: a keyed_set_add tag is exactly the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot, so no payload member ever enters set identity.

action.description: Optional finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family entry that the decision verb maps to (content-moderation.md §8.1).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for the report. Defaults to the Realm scope when absent; Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

provenance.description: Delivery provenance. Absent or "self" is a native self-authored report. "mimi_facade" is a service-attested report authored by the authorized receiving facade service after authenticating the source Provider and the reporter's claim and current authority. The facade never writes the reporter Actor as Event actor; source_provider_id is required only for mimi_facade.

source_provider_id.description: Origin MIMI provider's service DID for a facade-mapped report. Required exactly when provenance is "mimi_facade"; forbidden otherwise.

morph_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Morph object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance. stage and stage_changed_at are forbidden on create; the optional business stage axis is initialized only by ak.morph.stage.set.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

morph_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.stage.set. Mutates Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/morph.md §2.

not.$comment: Stage-set guard shared by the concrete Strand and Morph payload classes.

morph_update_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.update. Patches ordinary Morph fields on the Morph identified by target_ref. morph_kind is create-locked by ak.morph.create and MUST NOT appear in patch; stage and stage_changed_at are single-sourced by ak.morph.stage.set.

object_lifecycle_payload.description: Generic lifecycle payload for the Strand / Circle / Morph archive-restore-tombstone kinds. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref. The payload does NOT carry the target state: zh/models/common-fields.md section 5.2 maps the event kind itself to the state -- archive -> archived, restore -> active, tombstone -> tombstoned -- and the reducer produces it through the object_lifecycle_state derivation. An author-suppliable target state would put the object's `state` member, which universal_forbidden_patch_paths reserves for the reducer, back inside the author region through a second door, and would make ak.circle.archive able to spell a restore.

organization_moderation_policy_state_pay.description: Closed Organization moderation-policy state. organization_id is the Organization did_core_id and the sole registered typed current result subject; value carries the sole v1 Organization moderation-policy family.

participant_binding.description: Token issuer's signed commitment over (realm_id, call_id, focus_id, actor_id, device_id, participant_id, expires_at) for a media participant. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3 and crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1. v1 uses the single scheme ak.media.participant_binding.v1.

issuer_kid.description: DID URL (with fragment) of the token issuer service signing key. MUST resolve to a service DID present in the current-epoch ak.realm.media_service.service_id.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service may receive. Human-readable purposes do not replace this field.

policy_action_state_payload.description: Closed policy action-log payload. Exactly one policy_id or action_id is present and selects one of two tagged policy_action typed current result subject branches; the two namespaces never coalesce. value carries the sole v1 approval-action document family.

policy_set_state_payload.description: Closed Policy definition state payload. policy_id is the stable policy typed current result subject. value.schema selects exactly one of the two v1 Policy document families directly in this schema; unknown families fail schema validation.

profile_realm_override_payload.description: Realm-scoped actor profile override payload for ak.profile.realm_override. target_ref is the Actor Profile being overridden; target_realm_id is the Realm where the override applies. resolution, principal_id and actor_kind are forbidden here for the same reasons they are forbidden on the generic profile write surface -- a per-Realm override is still not a place to rebind identity; the object-specific forbidden path set is machine-indexed in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional guard over the folded current override: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the display object obtained by applying every accepted assertion patch of this target in accepted commit order to {} ({} when there is none), zh/sync/current-results.md section 2. A mismatch rejects with zero writes.

reaction_payload.description: Reducer input for ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove. The typed current result is a core authority-ordered keyed set of reaction assertions and both kinds project one keyed_set_add; default-view membership is keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key), and a remove tombstones every add from the same actor with the same key that is not strictly causally later than it, which includes the adds concurrent with it.
