See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8 for the authoritative Reaction model (target scope, authority-ordered keyed set, authz, anti-abuse) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.8 for the plaintext-vs-encrypted policy.

key.description: Reaction key. Plaintext scopes SHOULD use a single Unicode emoji cluster or registered short tag. End-to-end-encrypted scopes MUST carry the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag here and carry the equivalent base64url tag in encrypted_payload.encryption_context.routing_context. The exact standard MLS derivation is routing_root[N] = MLS-Exporter("ak.reaction-routing-root-v1", canonical_effective_scope_key_bytes(effective_scope), KDF.Nh), then ExpandWithLabel(routing_root[N], "ak.reaction-routing-v1", JCS({effective_scope,target_ref,routing_window}), 32), followed by HMAC-SHA256 over NFC(canonical_emoji). routing_window is derived from outer Event.created_at and does not require an hourly MLS Commit. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.8. The canonical emoji travels only in encrypted_payload.

annotation.description: Optional free-form annotation (e.g. issue triage label). MUST be omitted when `encrypted_payload` is present; in E2EE realms the annotation MUST instead be carried inside `encrypted_payload`.

encrypted_payload.description: Encrypted carrier for the canonical reaction key and any annotation in E2EE realms. The decrypted plaintext JSON MUST validate as #/$defs/reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext. When present, outer plaintext `key` MUST be the routing tag and `annotation` MUST be omitted; service-side authority-ordered keyed set convergence still uses the outer routing key.

read_receipt_policy_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.read_receipt_policy. Closed object so typos cause schema_violation. The enclosing Event carries realm_id; payload does not duplicate it. minProperties=1 rejects an empty no-op policy. Realm links and source Realm policies do not create a parent compliance floor. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.1.

alias.description: Canonical realm alias <localpart>:<domain> (zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3). Sigil-free: the display forms #general:acme.example and general@acme.example MUST NOT reach the wire. <domain> is the issuing authority and MUST be an authority domain of this Realm's trust_domain; a foreign-domain claim MUST be rejected with reason realm_alias_authority_mismatch.

realm_alias_payload.description: Closed payload for ak.realm.alias, the ONLY wire carrier of a Realm alias. A declaration writes the complete canonical alias; {tombstone:true} is a durable value tombstone that removes the alias from effective resolution without erasing the typed current result history. realm-genesis.schema.json and realm-profile.schema.json are closed and have no alias property, and ak.realm.create / ak.realm.profile payloads MUST NOT carry one.

realm_create_payload.description: Minimal identity and security-root payload for ak.realm.create. User-visible, mutable, policy and reducer-derived Realm state is carried only by registered bootstrap facets. Every genesis, including Principal Control Realm and Agent PCR, requires a canonical 32-octet genesis_salt.

realm_organization_payload.description: Organization-side endorsement or revocation for a Realm relationship. Reducer validation MUST require realm_id to match the top-level Event.realm_id, organization_id to identify an Organization principal in accepted registration state, the Realm-side writer to hold ak.realm.admin, and authorization to verify against current organization DID control evidence or a delegated service whose purpose covers this relationship and control_scopes. The stable organization_id is not itself resolvable DID material.

statement_id.description: Stable id of this organization statement. It is audit identity, not the reducer typed current result subject; the reducer typed current result subject is (organization_id, relationship).

realm_id.description: Realm the organization statement is bound to. MUST equal the enclosing Event.realm_id.

organization_id.description: Stable Organization principal identity that endorses, governs, sponsors, certifies, or revokes the Realm relationship. This did_core_id is bound to current Organization DID evidence through accepted registration/resolution state; it is not itself resolvable.

relationship.description: Relationship being asserted or revoked for this organization and Realm.

control_scopes.description: Machine-readable scopes covered by the organization's consent. A scope here is an endorsement boundary only; actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy, governance-Station authority, capability, or service-binding Event.

expires_at.description: Administrative review/renewal hint only. It does not auto-transition account status; a later AccountStatusRecord is required and remains subject to sequence and terminal rules.

realm_commit_ref.description: Optional RealmCommitId naming the authority commit whose current Realm state the organization evaluated when issuing this statement.

organization_policy_ref.description: Optional DID-document delegation URL, policy object, governance decision, or attestation reference used to evaluate the statement.

authorization.description: Organization-side authorization proof. This is independent of the Realm-side ak.realm.admin authorization required to write the event into Realm history.

issuer_id.description: Stable Organization or delegated-service principal identity that issued this statement. The issuer_id is a did_core_id; verification_method and accepted registration/delegation state carry the DID evidence required to verify the issuer.

delegation_ref.description: Required when issuer_role is governance_service or account_authority. It MUST resolve to a live organization DID delegation whose purpose covers ak.realm.organization and the requested relationship/control_scopes.

executed_by.description: Optional exact ActorId of the human administrator or service actor that initiated the organization-side decision. This does not become the organization principal.

proof.description: Signature, threshold transcript, or governance-service attestation over the canonical organization statement binding statement_id, realm_id, organization_id, relationship, status, control_scopes, issued_at, validity window, and statement replacement/revocation fields.

realm_owner_transfer_payload.description: ak.realm.owner.transfer — rotate the controller binding of the Realm authority-root typed current result. It changes controller_actor_id and increments controller_epoch only: authority_generation, the typed current result ref and every existing grant are untouched, so the whole authority tree issued by the previous controller stays valid. This is not a reparent — the root never moves.

expected_state_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the authority-root typed current result value this Event expects to replace. The reducer MUST compare-and-swap against it and reject a stale value rather than overwrite.

controller_actor_id.description: Exact ActorId of the successor that becomes the root controller. Its control proof MUST bind this complete identity; a bare principal DID or parallel Station sidecar is insufficient.

patch.description: The authority-root member selected by the author. The reducer also increments controller_epoch from the CAS-frozen pre-state; every other member is preserved verbatim.

successor_acceptance.description: Independent acceptance proof from the successor. The current controller proof, this proof, the payload and expected_state_digest MUST all enter the same signing transcript. The successor controller_epoch is uniquely computed from the expected pre-state, so neither party signs a producer-supplied counter.

realm_policy_bundle_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.policy_bundle — the payload IS this flat closed object (not a state wrapper); event-envelope.schema.json dispatches the kind directly to this def. The closed property set is the complete set of Realm policy facets that have no independent Event kind. Facets that DO have their own kind and typed current result (ak.realm.join_rule, ak.realm.history_access, ak.realm.read_receipt_policy, ak.realm.asset_privacy_policy, ak.realm.media_service, ak.realm.plaintext_visible_services, ...) MUST NOT be echoed here. Policy documents are carried only by ak.policy.set.
realm_policy_bundle_payload.description: Enabled Realm policy component set, written wholesale into the realm_policy_bundle commit-ordered projection typed current result: every revision restates the complete enabled component set and the Realm object's derived policy fields re-derive from the latest accepted bundle. policy_revision starts at 1 and every later authoritative reducer admission MUST equal previous.policy_revision + 1: rollback uses top-level policy_revision_rollback; a forward gap uses failed_precondition with reason_code policy_revision_gap and produces zero typed-current-result writes. policy_revision MUST cover policy_revision (see contract-registry event-kind row and models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3).

policy_revision.description: Strictly monotonic bundle revision; rollback or gaps are rejected.

federation_policy.description: The sole producer carrier of the effective Realm federation policy. High-assurance Realm reducers require closed, restricted, or quarantine and reject open.

media_service_decrypts.description: Whether a media service listed in plaintext_visible_services may decrypt call media. Defaults to false when absent. It is one of three conditions that MUST all hold (ak.realm.media_service declaration + plaintext_visible_services grant + this toggle). Because it changes who may receive media keys, it enters the media scope key_access_revision; a generation that does not cover the current value cannot authorize media decryption. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 8.2.

handle_issuer_policies.description: Ordered Realm handle-issuer trust policy used by primary-handle resolution. Earlier entries have higher tie-break priority; every issuer is domain-scoped.

member_action.description: How this Realm disposes of a principal's membership when the account enters deactivated. Defaults to leave_self_initiated when the component is absent. Unrecognized values fail closed to retain_membership with a policy parse warning and MUST NOT silently fall back to the default. The single authority for the closed enum and its disposition semantics is identity/account-lifecycle.md section 7.1.

consent_required.description: When true, every invite into this Realm MUST pass the holder consent admission gate in identity/consent-model.md section 6.1 before the invite Event is submitted. It MUST NOT be read as permission for a cross-Realm authority-commit precondition.

allowed_third_party_invite_verification_.description: Complete current allow-set of service DIDs trusted to attest 3PID ownership for ak.invite.third_party / ak.invite.claim. The array is whole-value replacement state in this policy-bundle revision, not an incremental patch. Absence and [] both deny every third-party invite verification service. Removing a DID in a later policy_revision revokes it for every later claim re-check; no separate tombstone exists. Reducers MUST evaluate the current accepted bundle typed current result on a fresh basis before accepting ak.invite.claim.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

realm_set_default_strand_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.set_default_strand. Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. Reducer projects strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify strand_id references a projected, non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm; a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. The Strand projection is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage. expected_default_strand_id compiles to a typed current result expected_revision precondition for optimistic concurrency (CAS). Absent and explicit null are normalized to the same null value before comparison, so omission asserts expected_revision null and is only valid while the typed current result is still in its initial no-default state; once a default is set the field MUST be present, otherwise the reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition and MUST NOT overwrite unconditionally.

expected_default_strand_id.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard compared as a whole value after absent and explicit null are normalized to null. The reducer accepts the write only if the Realm's current default_strand_id equals this value (null asserts no default is currently set). Omission therefore asserts expected_revision null and MUST fail once a default exists. Mismatch MUST be rejected (failed_precondition).

relation_create_payload.description: Create or replace the Relation current value at one registered primary conflict domain. primary_conflict_domain is the signed typed-current-result subject and MUST exactly match payload.relation's registered relation_kind/from_ref/to_ref shape. payload.relation is the closed six-field relation_definition authoring region; its optional relation.rank is the only create-time rank carrier, and materialized Relation members are forbidden. expected_revision is null only when the domain has never been written; after a tombstone, a new event-derived RelationId MAY replace that tombstoned value only at its exact revision. An active current value cannot be replaced by create.

relation_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.relation.tombstone. primary_conflict_domain is the signed typed-current-result subject; relation_id MUST equal the current value's id at that domain, and expected_revision MUST equal its exact revision. The transition is irreversible for that RelationId. When supplied, reason is retained on the Event and is not copied into the materialized Relation object.

relation_update_payload.description: Relation patch payload. primary_conflict_domain is the signed typed-current-result subject; relation_id MUST equal the current value's id at that domain, and expected_revision MUST equal its exact revision. relation_kind/from_ref/to_ref are create-locked because they define the subject; changing them requires an explicit tombstone followed by create. effective_scope and every effective_scope.* descendant path remain reducer-managed.

rsvp_encrypted_response.description: Encrypted RSVP response envelope. The content_type is pinned so a receiver can route the ciphertext to exactly one decrypted schema; the plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response.

rsvp_entry.description: Complete RSVP typed current result value. The whole entry is the current-value projection set value, so the deterministic winner carries the schedule source the responder observed plus the response itself.

schedule_basis_refs.description: The unique schedule revision the responder actually observed, retained in the existing array wire shape as exactly one ak:event: typed id. It is the sole carrier of that association: the payload holds exactly one entry, so no envelope mirror is required and none is defined. Shape admission is decidable from this field alone, without resolving the referenced Event.

response.description: Plaintext response branch. Only admissible while the target Strand scope has no accepted ak.mls.genesis and the receiving service declares the rsvp_response plaintext data class; after activation it MUST be rejected with mls_activation_required.

encrypted_response.description: Encrypted response branch; content_type is pinned to application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json and the decrypted plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response. Required once the target Strand scope has an accepted ak.mls.genesis.

rsvp_response.description: RSVP response object. Used directly by rsvp_entry.response and as the decrypted plaintext of rsvp_entry.encrypted_response, whose content_type is application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json. status and comment always share one encryption boundary; a plaintext status with an encrypted comment is not a valid shape.

comment.description: Optional responder comment. An empty response is expressed by omitting the field, never by an empty string.

event_ref.description: Calendar event Strand id; encoded as a ak:strand: typed id.

occurrence.description: JSON null for the whole series, or the canonical recurrence instance key: YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events and YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[Zone] for timed events. The date component MUST be a real proleptic-Gregorian date, not merely match the digit pattern. The producer MUST canonicalize before signing; receivers MUST reject non-canonical keys instead of rewriting them.

schema_define_state_payload.description: Schema definition payload. value is a JSON Schema 2020-12 document validated by the executable ak.validator.json_schema_2020_12_definition.v1 profile; value.$id is the stable definition typed current result subject.

sidecar_context_attach_payload.description: Controller-signed versioned attachment of a source Realm context to an existing native Sidecar. It creates no Strand or Relation protocol object.

sidecar_create_payload.description: Minimal native Sidecar genesis intent. The payload is empty: sidecar_id is derived from the Event id; realm_id, controller_account_id, state and timestamps are reducer-derived from the accepted envelope, and the Sidecar scope activates standard RFC 9420 through its own accepted ak.mls.genesis.

space_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Space object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

space_object_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.tombstone. Realm tombstone uses its separate Realm lifecycle payload; Space tombstone targets payload.space_id.

space_parent_payload.description: Reparent one Space. All three members are required. parent_space_id is nullable and explicit null is the one spelling of "no parent" on this payload, so the space_parent register stays total and an omitted member can never mean the root by accident; the Space create object spells the same fact by absence and the genesis write normalizes it. expected_parent_space_id is the declared prior parent this producer read, not an optional compare-and-set: zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 3.5 registers it as a pre_state requirement on the space_parent family, and making it optional would give one Event kind two admission semantics selected by a member's presence.

space_patch_payload.description: Space metadata patch and optional separate child scope policy command. A policy member selects security execution; the patch cannot touch policy, identity, scope or lifecycle, including dotted paths. A combined Event is atomic and requires security finality.

space_state_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.archive and ak.space.restore. The target Space is expressed on payload.space_id; top-level target_ref is a rejected field on Event envelopes.

realm_media_service_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.media_service. The media descriptor lives under payload.value (a state_payload envelope), never flattened onto payload. This def is closed on purpose: the descriptor is the trust root for media token issuance (service_id, ice_config_endpoint and every foci[].token_endpoint per zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 2.1), and it was previously typed only as the open state_payload, which let a deployment carry provider-specific token issuer configuration inside a signed Realm policy typed current result while a spec-shaped consumer read nothing at all. Issuer configuration -- signing key ids, token audiences, TTLs, backend API credentials -- is deployment configuration of the service named by foci[].token_endpoint. It MUST NOT be carried here: putting it in the typed current result would make an issuer key rotation require a Realm policy Event holding ak.realm.media_service or ak.policy.manage capability, and would publish issuer internals to every Realm member. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 2.

service_id.description: Media service principal. Every issued participant_binding.issuer_kid and service_signature.kid MUST project onto this DID (media-service-binding.md section 3).

ice_config_endpoint.description: ICE / TURN credential endpoint. Part of the section 2.1 integrity binding.

foci.description: Non-empty multi-focus list. A descriptor carrying a single flat sfu_endpoint, or no foci at all, MUST fail closed with media_service_foci_required; a server MUST NOT normalize or infer one in the realtime path.

media_service_focus.$comment: One backend focus. focus_id and focus_kind identify it; token_endpoint and connect_url are what a client actually needs to join, so both are required rather than optional -- a focus a client cannot exchange a token at, or cannot connect to, is not a usable focus and must fail schema validation instead of failing at join time. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 2.

focus_id.description: Stable focus id inside this Realm media service. It enters the signed canonical bytes and the session_focus election (call-state.md section 4.1).

focus_kind.description: Backend binding id. It sits on the kind axis rather than being spelled `type`, because the value set is an Arkret-owned closed registry and classification-field-registry.json reserves the type axis for fields inherited verbatim from an external standard. Only livekit and arkret_native have a normative binding in v1; a client meeting an unknown or unsupported focus_kind MUST fail closed with unknown_focus_type rather than hand the token to an arbitrary SDK.

token_endpoint.description: Token exchange endpoint (section 3). Shared abstraction across every backend; only backend_token differs. Part of the section 2.1 trust root, so a client MUST verify the exact typed current result value against the current confirmed RealmCommit state before anchoring it.

connect_url.description: Backend connection entry point; the concrete protocol is fixed by the type-specific binding appendix.

health_endpoint.description: Client pre-flight endpoint, usable only for ordering foci_preferred before a session_focus is committed. Once call_focus carries a session_focus, a connect failure MUST surface as focus unavailable and MUST NOT silently switch focus.

cascade_group.description: Backend cluster this focus belongs to, for user-visible disclosure that a cross-region conference is cascaded inside the backend. The protocol does not standardize SFU-to-SFU cascading.

realm_discovery_payload.description: Closed whole-value payload for ak.realm.discovery. Preview field selection is owned exclusively by ak.realm.preview_policy.

realm_schema_payload.description: Closed whole-value payload for ak.realm.schema. value.schema_refs is the complete replacement set of activated schema ids; it is not merged with any previous set. Every member MUST be a registered ak.schema.*.vN id, and the core member ak.schema.realm.v1 MUST be present in every update, so the set can never drop self-contained Realm validation. The Realm structural role is carried only by the signed ak.schema.realm_genesis.v1 purpose and is not writable here; policy and deployment profiles have their own carriers.

schema_refs.description: Complete replacement set of activated schema ids. Members MUST be registered ak.schema.*.vN ids; unknown or unregistered ids fail closed. ak.schema.realm.v1 MUST be a member of every accepted value.

strand_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the Strand object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance. stage and stage_changed_at are forbidden on create; the optional business stage axis is initialized only by ak.strand.stage.set.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, strand_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the current-value projection value as 'list_space_id' on the typed current result at ak:result:strand_position:<board_space_id>:<strand_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ak.strand.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

strand_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.update. Patches ordinary Strand fields on the Strand identified by target_ref.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

strand_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.stage.set. Mutates Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/strand-and-message.md §3.2.

not.$comment: Stage-set guard shared by the concrete Strand and Morph payload classes. Reason-style fields are forbidden; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message.

strand_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.strand.watch.set. Writes the (strand_id, watcher_actor_id) watch typed current result. The new typed current result value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST have one same-batch ak.audit.accessed event pointing to the watch Event with semantic_refs[role=audit_pair], and its payload access_kind=watch_set_others must bind writer_actor_id, target_actor_id, target_ref=strand_id and paired_event_id. The Station validates current watch state and atomically commits both Events; no caller-authored result head is carried. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the typed current result (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Ordinary watch predicate evaluated only against the signed causal basis. null asserts an unwritten basis; a concrete value must match the selected exact base head. It does not serialize independent offline writes or pick a winner.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a typed current result does not carry a public-level setting).

track_name.description: Strand track key carried by Message Event payloads. In v1 Message payloads are restricted to 'discussion'; the materialized Message resolves its track through the referenced Strand and does not duplicate this payload-only field.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a concrete verification method. Bare DIDs are not valid where a key binding is required.

view_reconcile_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.reconcile. view_id is the view typed current result subject -- zh/models/views.md section 3.2 is normative that all three View kinds write ONE family, so the family is named for the View, not for this payload. definition is the complete author-editable definition (view.schema.json #/$defs/view_definition), not an author-overwritable copy of the materialized object: identity, Realm, schema, creation metadata and lifecycle state are retained from the target pre-state, and update provenance is derived from this Event. Reconcile is neither create object snapshot nor update patch: it replaces the definition wholesale.

relation_create_object.description: Relation create input: the closed six-field authoring region of relation.schema.json, not the materialized object. Its optional rank is the only create-time rank carrier. See that definition for why reducer-owned members are absent.

expected_governance_generation.description: Station tenure the producer observed. The handoff is a compare-and-set on the governing Station tenure, never on the Realm authority-root delegation generation.

device_authorize_applet_managed_possessi.description: Candidate-device possession transcript of the applet_managed_delegation branch. The signing input is UTF8("ak.device_authorize_applet_managed_possession_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json(this object); the signature it produces is the payload's device_signature, which is why device_signature is not a member here. It adds applet_id, the exact Applet install whose accepted managed-actor provision created this principal and therefore the device's revocation fence, and it narrows expires_at and scopes to non-null because the payload requires both on this branch. recovery_session_id is the normalized null.

device_authorize_possession_transcript.description: Candidate-device possession transcript of the registration_anchor branch: the second Event of a PCR genesis unit. The signing input is UTF8("ak.device_authorize_possession_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json(this object); the signature it produces is the payload's device_signature, which is why device_signature is not a member here. authorized_generation_ref is fixed to 1, the value the same pcr_genesis_unit initializes. recovery_session_id and scopes are the normalized nulls of a branch whose payload carries neither.

device_authorize_recovery_possession_tra.description: Candidate-device possession transcript of the pcr_recovery branch. The signing input is UTF8("ak.device_authorize_recovery_possession_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json(this object); the signature it produces is the payload's device_signature, which is why device_signature is not a member here. recovery_session_id is narrowed to the non-null accepted recovery session, so the transcript cannot be replayed outside the unit that authorized it, and authorized_generation_ref MUST equal the sibling ak.device.reanchor new_device_generation.

realm_authority_reset_payload.description: ak.realm.authority.reset — invalidate every capability grant that descends from this Realm's authority root in one accepted Event. It increments authority_generation only: controller_actor_id and controller_epoch are preserved verbatim, so the reset is not a controller change and never moves the root. Every realm_root grant ref carries the generation it was issued under, so advancing the generation is exactly what makes a whole delegated authority tree stop evaluating; ak.realm.owner.transfer preserves the generation and therefore leaves every child grant valid. The current controller is the only possible author: the compare-and-set below requires the frozen pre-state digest, so this is a deliberate act by the holder of root control, never an automatic takeover of a lost authority.

expected_state_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the authority-root typed current result value this Event expects to replace. The reducer MUST compare-and-swap against it and reject a stale value rather than overwrite. The successor generation is uniquely computed from the pre-state this digest freezes, so no counter is carried on the wire.

view_create_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.create. zh/models/views.md section 3.2 gives the three View kinds three different author loads over one typed current result family; one shared def with an anyOf of the three branches and no event_kind discriminator admitted every shape on every kind -- an ak.view.update could carry an unconstrained definition object, and an ak.view.create could carry {view_id, patch}. Each kind now binds exactly one closed payload.

object.description: ak.view.create author definition: the same closed authoring region ak.view.reconcile replaces wholesale, NOT the materialized object. The earlier shape was the materialized View minus four banned members, which still handed the author schema, realm_id, created_by, created_at and state -- the create-locked members every later write retains verbatim, so a self-reported creator or realm became permanent truth, and a create could start a View outside its initial state. Those five are now produced by the registered create-lock derivations of zh/models/common-fields.md section 3.3, which also removes the prose-only cross-check that created_by and created_at had to equal the envelope: there is nothing left to cross-check when the reducer is the only writer.

view_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.update: the incremental patch surface, and the only shared-View removal path (zh/models/views.md section 3.1). It MUST NOT carry an object snapshot or a whole definition -- those are create and reconcile -- and view_id is required because it is the typed current result subject.

expected_state_digest.description: Signed frozen pre-state guard. It names the exact committed current value this patch was authored against: the single value the target typed current result holds at the position the write is applied, per the accepted order of its own stream. A mismatch fails the Event; it MUST NOT be resolved by choosing an older historical candidate that does match. contract-registry.json registers nothing for it because the v1 result_projection grammar has no expected_prestate member, so it is an admission rule beside the projection rather than part of it.

device_authorize_recovery_session_id.description: Accepted recovery session this device authorization is admitted beside. One form, referenced by the device_authorize_payload member and by the possession core so the transcript cannot drift to a second spelling.

device_authorize_possession_core.description: Shared signing-input core of the three candidate-device possession transcripts: registration_anchor, pcr_recovery and applet_managed_delegation. This object is not a wire member of any Event: it is the object the candidate device signs, and the signing input is UTF8("<domain>\n") || canonical_json(this object) with canonical_json per conformance/encoding.md section 2 (JCS) and <domain> the variant's x-arkret-signature-domain. The resulting signature is what the ak.device.authorize payload then carries as device_signature, so this core MUST NOT contain device_signature, any Event id, any Event or envelope digest, pairing_challenge_transcript_digest or any other proof material: those are outputs of this transcript or carriers for it, and signing them would be circular. account_id is present and is injected from the Event envelope actor_id rather than mirrored by the closed payload. Every authorization member the payload may omit is required here and normalized to null, so 'absent' and 'present as null' cannot both encode the same authorization (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.1). The core is deliberately not closed; each registered variant closes itself with unevaluatedProperties false after narrowing its branch, so exactly the members that variant registers may appear.

account_id.description: Complete account AccountId subject of the ak.device.authorize Event this transcript authorizes, injected from that Event envelope's account actor_id. It is NOT a payload member: device_authorize_payload is closed and MUST NOT mirror a principal_id or an account_id, so a verifier MUST rebuild this member from the envelope actor_id.account_id it already authenticated and MUST NOT take it from a payload member, a route, a session audience or any unsigned body member.

device_id.description: Candidate device identity, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.device_id.

device_public_key_did.description: Candidate device Ed25519 signing key in did:key form, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.device_public_key_did. It is the key that verifies this transcript's own signature.

hpke_key.description: Candidate device HPKE public key, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.hpke_key. Signing it here is what forbids a service from substituting it.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.algorithms. The producer MUST sort and deduplicate them by UTF-8 bytewise order before signing.

authorized_by.description: Byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.authorized_by. Under registration_anchor it MUST equal account_id.principal_id; that is an equality between two members of this same object, which JSON Schema cannot express, so it is a normative requirement of crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.1 that the accepting side checks. Under pcr_recovery the same principal is selected by the accepted recovery policy and the account-local lineage, not by current DID controller state. Under applet_managed_delegation it is the Applet-managed principal's own principal_id.

authorization_binding_kind.description: The branch this transcript is signed for. accepted_device is absent by construction: that branch's candidate signs device-pairing.schema.json#/$defs/device_pairing_target_proof under its own domain instead, because at stage time it does not yet know the approving sibling. A verifier MUST select the domain from this member and MUST NOT accept a transcript reused across binding kinds.

authorized_generation_ref.description: PCR-local device generation this authorization is bound to, byte-equal to device_authorize_payload.authorized_generation_ref. The candidate device signs it, so a relay cannot move an authorization to another generation without invalidating this signature (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.5.2).

expires_at.description: Required here and null when the payload omits it. Making it required is what makes the section 5.2.1 normalization executable: if it were optional, an omitted member and an explicit null would be two canonical byte strings for one authorization and the normalization could not be enforced.

scopes.description: Required here and null when the payload omits it, for the same reason as expires_at.

recovery_session_id.description: Required here; non-null only on the pcr_recovery branch and normalized to null on the two branches whose payload forbids the member.
